overview_markdown:
Spacebot is an opinionated agent harness written in Rust, from the team behind Spacedrive, designed explicitly for teams, communities, and multi-user environments. Its core thesis is that agent state belongs in structured storage rather than markdown files managed by the LLM: memory lives in a typed graph in SQLite, conversation history compacts into durable 'chronicles', and autonomy runs on a task state machine linked to goals. The LLM reasons while the system holds state.

Architecturally, Spacebot splits the monolithic agent loop into specialized processes — conversation, memory persistence, compaction, and ingestion run independently, so the agent can keep talking while background work proceeds. Recent commits show active hardening: a prompt inspector that records and decomposes every LLM request into block maps, context-ceiling enforcement applied per-model at request time, and skill capture that lets the agent accumulate reusable knowledge across sessions.

Compared to OpenClaw, Spacebot targets a different niche: concurrent multi-user deployments (Discord communities, Slack workspaces) with shared memory, plus an optional hosted one-click deploy at spacebot.sh. It trades OpenClaw's massive ecosystem and permissive licensing for a more opinionated, state-first design under the FSL-1.1-ALv2 license.
